review.identity: The original test's metadata assertions distinguish read-only prewarm from danger-full-access sampling; unchanged submit_turn explicitly selects PermissionProfile::Disabled. The exact source compatibility projection removes the prewarm phase and volatile turn lineage but retains sandbox and sandbox_mode, and WebsocketConnectionIdentity compares the serialized projection. The fixture must admit the resulting new connection.
review.fixture_liveness: The original server serially consumes one scripted connection before accepting another. Leaving the prewarm connection waiting for later sampling requests prevents accepting the identity-changing socket. Closing only the one-request prewarm script permits acceptance; the actual three-request sampling script remains open until explicit shutdown.
review.within_turn: The second test's original three response batches remain byte-token identical and all execute on connection index 1. Exact [1,3] plus unchanged [null,ts-1,ts-1] assertions still reject sampling reconnections and later metadata overriding the first state. The added first batch supplies only the otherwise missing generate=false prewarm response.
review.across_turns: The first test retains all four original response batches. Exact [1,3] proves first sampling, tool follow-up and next logical turn share the second physical connection. The original turn-state sequence, request_kind, generate, sandbox_mode and same/different turn-ID assertions remain unchanged after flattening the two connection logs.
review.limits: Closing the prewarm script can itself force reconnection, so [1,3] alone does not prove that production compatibility identity requires it. That requirement is separately supported by the unchanged projection and permission-selection source. These tests retain same-turn and cross-turn sampling connection coverage; they do not independently qualify prewarm reuse under identical permissions.
